studyArea.name: Seven Lakes of San Pablo City, Laguna
studyArea.assignmentLimit: The chapter states that fish sampling took place in each lake and reports per-lake sample totals. Its narrative gives only partial taxon-by-lake statements. The cluster linkage documents the surveyed waterbodies, not a complete species inventory or current occurrence.

bibliography.title: Ecological Carrying Capacity Modeling and Sustainability Assessment of the Seven Lakes of San Pablo City, Laguna, Philippines
bibliography.book: Ecosystem and Species Habitat Modeling for Conservation and Restoration

method.fishSampling: The chapter says gill nets were used to assess fish composition and abundance; wild fish samples were collected per lake with local fisherfolk. Horizontally oriented nets with different mesh sizes were set at 5:00 PM and retrieved at 7:00 AM.
method.samplingPeriod: July-August 2019, described by the chapter as the onset of the wet season.
method.identificationReferences: The chapter lists fish-identification references including Herre, Vidthayanon, Froese and Pauly, Fitzgerald, Behrends et al., Wu et al., and Herder et al.
method.limits: The reviewed text does not provide a fish-by-station table, fish-net coordinates, exact mesh sizes, net dimensions, standardized effort by lake, voucher identifiers, specimen catalog crosswalk, or reusable machine-readable data. Water-quality station figures are not treated as fish-net coordinates.

partialTaxonByLakeNarrative.scope: The narrative says these samples largely represented the total collected fish; it supplies no per-lake counts for this label.
The narrative names these lakes but gives no per-lake counts. The two unmentioned lakes are not treated as absences.

otherFigureCaptionTaxonLabels: Vieja sp. (mixed red and green flowerhorn)
sourceStatements.figureCaptionLimit: Figure 25.29 captions these as fish samples collected from the Seven Lakes collectively; the caption does not map every label to a particular lake. The chapter's narrative uses Amphilophus sp. for red devil while this caption labels Vieja sp. forms, so the conflict is retained rather than taxonomically resolved.
sourceStatements.communityKnowledgeLane: The chapter separately presents a participatory rural appraisal and a community-perceived fish composition table. Those perceptions, including the narrative about dalag in several lakes, are not merged into the gill-net sample results or treated as verified catches.
sourceStatements.introductionLead: The chapter separately reports a first 2017 report of Vieja sp. in Bunot, Calibato, Mohicap, and Palakpakin and says the introduction mechanism was not recorded. This is not a 2019 gill-net assignment or evidence of a current population.
sourceStatements.diet: No fish diet or gut-content result was identified in the reviewed fish-survey sections.

rights.publisherAccess: Springer identifies this as subscription content and offers an institutional-access route or paid chapter purchase.
rights.reviewedCopy: ResearchGate lists a public full-text file uploaded by coauthor Joseph De Guzman Campang on 12 March 2026, labels it author content, and warns that content may be subject to copyright. The chapter front matter states that the author(s) licensed the work exclusively to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. in 2023.
rights.decision: No local copy, image, table, or figure was retained. Record only citation/provenance and bounded research notes. No item-specific grant for Bangwit species-profile or app reuse was verified; publication approval is not granted.

limitations: The 620 fish and per-lake totals are historical study sample counts, not present abundance, catch rates, or completeness estimates.
The named two-taxon lake associations are incomplete prose summaries and cannot be converted into absences for other lakes.
The cluster-wide specimen figure labels and community-perception table have different evidence bases; neither is a complete modern lake checklist.
The red-devil labels Amphilophus sp. and Vieja sp. conflict within the chapter and are not reconciled here.
No diet, current presence, catchability, legality, safety, or public-app reuse claim follows from this source review.
nextAction: Seek the article's underlying fish-by-lake/specimen data, identification or voucher crosswalk, and item-specific reuse permission. Cross-check each exact source taxon label with a current taxonomic authority before any separate research assertion; do not infer current presence or absence from this 2019 study.
